title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the page; earlier pages are not available. K is a field, probably the fraction field of a Dedekind (dimension-1) ring A, and E is a (probably central) simple K-algebra, plausibly a quaternion algebra. 𝒪 is a set of A-orders in E. B_1 is the 2-category (or bicategory) whose objects are orders σ, v ∈ 𝒪 and whose Hom(σ,v) is the groupoid of 'special' (invertible, 'torsor-like') (σ,v)-bimodules, composed by tensor product. B_0 is a 2-category of 'catégories de Deuring' C. These are presumably additive categories modelled on supersingular elliptic curves up to isogeny-type data. In such a category, for any object X, End_C(X) = σ is an order of 𝒪 with σ ⊗ K ≅ E.

Step 1, Condition (C). For σ, v ∈ 𝒪, the composition law on special bimodules, (L,M) ↦ L·M, is commutative: LM = ML. Grothendieck glosses this as a special case of a hypothesis about E whose wording is illegible. The margin notes the following:
- (C) holds in the dimension-1 case.
- In the local (complete) case, the relation LM = ML holds for bispecial bimodules over σ.

This matches the classical fact that invertible two-sided ideals of a maximal order form a free abelian group. In the local case they are just powers of the unique two-sided prime.

Step 2. Take C ∈ B_0 and X ∈ C, with σ = End_C(X) ∈ 𝒪 and a chosen identification E ≅ σ_K. A Morita-type equivalence α_X identifies the category of self-equivalences Eq(C) = Hom_{B_0}(C,C) with Hom_{B_1}(σ,σ), the Picard groupoid of special (σ,σ)-bimodules.

Step 3. Under (C), the target is a strict commutative Picard category. Its commutativity constraint is built as follows:
- Embed L ≅ L' ⊂ E and M ≅ M' ⊂ E as (σ,σ)-sub-bimodules (fractional two-sided ideals).
- Then L ⊗_σ M ≅ L'M' = M'L' ≅ M ⊗_σ L.

The constraint is then transported to Eq(C). The claim, whose proof is just beginning, is that the resulting symmetric Picard structure on Eq(C) does not depend on the choice of X.

Purpose. The aim is to give the band (lien) / automorphism 2-group of a Deuring category an abelian (strictly commutative) Picard structure. The likely use, within 'Galois theory of motives', is gerbe or H^2-type classification of such categories, for instance supersingular isogeny motives over finite fields, à la Giraud.

Note: the 'neighbouring pages' supplied (an implicit-function / power-series argument) clearly belong to a different document. They are irrelevant here.
errors: Condition (C) is false for general orders: two-sided invertible ideals of non-maximal orders need not commute. The margin only partially restricts it (dimension 1, local/complete case, bispecial bimodules), so the hypothesis must be imposed (e.g. maximal orders); it is not automatic.

Well-definedness of c is not checked on the page. It holds because the bimodule embeddings L → E are unique up to central scalars λ ∈ K* (when E is central). Changing the embeddings scales L'M' and M'L' by the same λμ, so c is independent of choices. Strictness (c_{L,L} = id) holds by using the same embedding twice. Naturality and the hexagon follow because everything takes place inside E.

Independence from the choice of X is asserted ('à priori') but its proof is only begun. Changing X conjugates through an invertible (σ,σ')-bimodule, and commutativity (C) for Hom(σ,σ') is what makes the transported constraint agree. The page stops before this verification.

ideas.what: Commutativity of the product of invertible two-sided bimodules (ideals) between orders in a simple algebra, used as a hypothesis (C)
ideas.modern_name: Commutativity of the group of two-sided ideals of maximal orders / Picard group of a maximal order
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical: Deuring, Eichler; Reiner 'Maximal Orders' (1975); Fröhlich 'The Picard group of noncommutative rings' (1973)

ideas.what: Autoequivalences of a 'Deuring category' ≃ Picard groupoid of invertible (σ,σ)-bimodules over σ = End(X) (Morita)
ideas.modern_name: Morita theory / Deuring correspondence as an equivalence of categories (supersingular curves ↔ invertible modules over a maximal quaternion order)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Morita, Bass (1960s); categorical Deuring correspondence: Kohel (1996), Voight 'Quaternion Algebras' ch. 42

ideas.what: Strict commutative Picard category structure on Eq(C), with commutativity constraint defined by embedding bimodules into E, transported to Eq(C) independently of X
ideas.modern_name: Strictly commutative Picard category / symmetric 2-group (band of a gerbe)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne SGA 4 XVIII §1.4 (1973); Sinh's thesis (1975, Grothendieck's student)
ideas.where_published: Picard categories are treated in SGA 4 XVIII (Deligne) and in Sinh's thesis; this specific construction is not known to be published

ideas.what: Abstract 2-category B_0 of 'catégories de Deuring' fibred over a 2-category B_1 of orders and special bimodules
ideas.modern_name: 2-categorical / gerbe-theoretic formulation of the Deuring correspondence (isogeny categories as gerbes or twisted forms)

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats Deuring-type categories (endomorphism rings = orders in a simple algebra, as for supersingular elliptic curves) as objects of a 2-category. Their automorphism 2-groups are strict commutative Picard categories of invertible bimodules, so that such categories can be classified by abelian gerbe / H^2 methods. The categorical Deuring correspondence in the later literature (Kohel, Voight, isogeny-based cryptography) is formulated 1-categorically, without this symmetric 2-group / band viewpoint.
missed.quote: la catégorie Eq(C)=Hom_{B_0}(C,C) est une cat. de Picard stricte ... indépendante à priori du choix de X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A canonical symmetric 2-group of autoequivalences of the supersingular isogeny category would give a natural framework for its twisted forms and descent, e.g. over non-closed finite fields, and for Galois-of-motives questions in the supersingular locus.

missed.claim: The independence of the commutativity constraint from the base object X, and the role of condition (C) for non-maximal orders, are left unproved or open on this page.
missed.quote: Je note (et il faudrait [vérifier]) ... que ce sont vrais dans les ... (dans le cas local ...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would determine for which order classes (Eichler, Gorenstein, ...) the Deuring 2-category has an abelian band. Those orders arise in level structures and in oriented supersingular isogeny graphs.

deep.surprise_reason: The ingredients are classical: Morita theory, commutativity of two-sided ideals of maximal orders, and strict Picard categories (Deligne/Sinh). Packaging the Deuring correspondence as a 2-category with a strictly commutative Picard band, with the explicit constraint built by embedding bimodules in E, is a nice unpublished detail. It is not a result a specialist would find startling.
transcription_corrections: 'catégorie de D[?]' should read 'catégorie de Deuring'.
The equivalence reads Hom_{B_0}(C,C) ≃^{α_X} Hom_{B_1}(σ,σ), not Hom_{B_1}(C,C).
'(un [?] de : tout motif de E est inversible)': 'motif' is doubtful; the hand reads more like '(un renforcement de : tout [idéal/ordre?] de E est inversible)'.
'ensemble des (v,v)-torseurs spéciaux': the correction is '(σ,v)-' bimodules/torseurs spéciaux.

'est formée une cat. de Picard stricte ... contrainte de commutativité, une [?] à priori du choix de X' is better read as '... munie d'une contrainte de commutativité, indépendante a priori du choix de X'.
